about: Real IdentityMD work records, byte for byte as served by https://api.imd.fun/work-records/<hash>.json (HTTP GET; none of them ends with a newline). Each is stored as hexadecimal text of those bytes (0x prefix, no newline), so that this folder holds data and no third-party prose: `python3 build_fixtures.py decode <file>` gives the JSON back, and `python3 build_fixtures.py check` re-derives this index from the files. recordHash is keccak256 of the decoded bytes (`cast keccak $(cat <file>)` prints it); onChainLatest is WorkRegistry.latest(jobId) read with `cast call` when the fixture was built. Expected values (hashes, offsets, agent ids) were derived by build_fixtures.py, outside the Solidity code, with a separate scanner cross-checked against Python's JSON parser. agentIds leaves out the agents whose only signals record a rejected submission (value 0); rejectedSignals counts those signals.
selection: Which records are stored, and why. 41 records were fetched and examined; all of them are listed under `observed` with their hash, kind, state and size, and any of them can be fetched again from https://api.imd.fun/work-records/<hash>.json and checked against WorkRegistry.latest. A record is stored when a test needs its bytes, and each stored record has a `role` saying what it is there for: the reference job; one small record for each job template, so that the scanner meets the shapes different templates produce; and one record for each property that only real data can show (a blocked job, a superseded first receipt and its successor, an agent named in two signals, rejected submissions, a record walked nearly to its end, a record too large for calldata). A record was left out when it was another instance of something a stored record already shows: two completed audits of 54 and 86 KB, a second impl_tests_review of 107 KB, a 43 KB multi_contract, a 31 KB adversarial review, and two more small blocked records. The kinds multi_contract and skill:adversarial-review therefore have no stored record; their kind strings and record hashes are in `observed`. The records hold other people's job text, which is why none is stored in readable form and why the set is kept to what is used.

fixtures.role: The reference job of README.md. Proven unchanged against the live registry by the fork suite, and the completed record the desk and pot tests put an order header into.

fixtures.role: A job that ended blocked and still has a receipt: the not-completed case, and the blocked record the tests put an order header into.

fixtures.note: Above 100 KB; has a parentJobId. Completed after a rejected first attempt: two signals, agent 51746 with value 0 (rejected in the record's own verification list) and agent 51620 with value 1. agentIds names only 51620.
fixtures.role: A record with a rejected submission among its signals (value 0): two signals, one agent named. Also the largest record that still fits one transaction's calldata; on the chunk path it needs five data contracts.

fixtures.note: A blocked launch build: the largest record stored here (317 KB), beyond one transaction, so only proveChunks reaches it. Six signals: four accepted submissions and two rejected ones (value 0, agents 51091 and 51006), which agentIds leaves out.
fixtures.role: The one record examined that is too large to send as calldata (318 KB): it can be proven only through data contracts, thirteen of them, and it is what the cost figures in WorkProof's notes were measured on. Also the one record with rejected submissions among several agents: six signals, two rejected, four agents named. A blocked job with signals.

fixtures.note: Kind research: its top-level research array (85 KB) sorts before schema, so the scan walks almost the whole record. The worst case for scanning cost.
fixtures.role: The costliest real proof: a research record whose bulk sorts before `state` and is walked nearly to the end. Pins the cost figure quoted in WorkProof.

fixtures.role: The research shape again, small and blocked.

fixtures.note: FIRST receipt of a job that later got a second one. It is no longer latest(jobId), so prove fails HashMismatch against the real registry.
